title: Increasing Triplet Subsequence
statement: Return true when there exist indices i < j < k with nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k].
hints: Track the smallest value so far and the smallest value that has a smaller predecessor.
Call them first and second, both starting at infinity.
If a value is bigger than second, it completes a triplet. If it is smaller than first, it becomes the new first. Otherwise, if it is between them, it becomes the new second.

approaches.name: Triple loop or LIS length
approaches.explanation: Stop when the LIS reaches length 3.

editorial: first is the smallest start seen. second is the smallest middle that already has a valid start somewhere before it, not necessarily first as it stands now. Updating first to a later smaller value does not invalidate second, because second's original start is still to its left. A value above second therefore has both a middle and a start before it.
